newsitem.title: UK: Euro oil swaps strengthen amid Iraq uncertainty.
newsitem.headline: Euro oil swaps strengthen amid Iraq uncertainty.

text.p: European oil swaps were broadly firmer on Monday as the energy complex faced uncertainty about the United Nations response to Iraq's food distribution plan, a precursor to resumed oil exports, following a Baghdad meeting between the two sides on Sunday.
U.N. officials declined to comment on the meeting.

Brent crude CFDs firmed by several cents with July 15-18 at -13 cents against September Brent from -17 cents and July 21-25 at -22 cents from -24 cents. July 28 to August 1 was assessed around -23 cents from -26 cents and August 4-8 was unchanged at -27 cents, also against September Brent.
July 14-18 was sold at -10 cents against August and again at -13 cents against September.
Heavy fuel swaps were also firmer, by 50 cents to $1.00 with little-talked July valued at $85.75, August at $86.75 and September at $87.50.
Wet barges were understood to have traded at $86.25 and $87.25 for fob Rotterdam stored material while refinery material was heard around $87.50.
Gasoline tacked up $2 or so a tonne as tight local supplies and strong U.S. prices acted as support. Dealers said August was around $188.00 from $186 on Friday.
Naphtha was also a couple of dollars stronger, taking comfort from gasoline and higher prices in Asia. Dealers said August was around $181.50, but business was fairly quiet.
Gas oil crack spreads were around $4.25 for 4Q97, $4.40 for 1Q98 and $4-4.05 for 2Q98.
